title: The Impact of Open Data on Public Procurement

evidence.description: README defines the four-stage SQL Server/Stata order and database/ODBC preparation.
evidence.quote:
The code in the zip folder converts the raw data into the final dataset used in the analysis. 

We compile the code using SQL Server 2017 and Stata 17 in the following order:
1- Data cleaning and sample preparation.sql
2- Clean Eurostat and Factiva data.do
3- Append variables.sql
4- Prepare analysis sample.do

Before running the code, we perform two steps:
We create an empty database titled “Procurement.” This is the working database in which the code writes SQL tables. 
We import each source of raw data in SQL Server as a separate database using the SQL Server Import Wizard. We name these databases using the following convention: Proc_[Data Source Name]. We treat the databases with the raw data as “read only” (i.e., the code only “writes” in the [Procurement] database).

evidence.description: README identifies the final Stata file as conditioning regression samples.
evidence.quote: The file titled “4- Prepare analysis sample.do” estimates a regression for each outcome variable in the main analysis, conditioning on the samples reported in the tables.

evidence.description: SQL preparation reads the Opentender Batch1 table and creates a contract key.
evidence.quote:
SELECT 			CONTRACT_ID = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY RECORD_ID),
				*
INTO			Opentender		
FROM			Proc_Opentender_Batch1.DBO.OpenTender_Batch1
;

evidence.description: SQL preparation reads TED contract-award notices with nonmissing offers.
evidence.quote:
SELECT 				ROW_NUMBER() 
OVER				(ORDER BY ID_NOTICE_CAN, LOTS_NUMBER) AS CONTRACT_LOT_ID_TED,
					*
INTO				TED_CLEANSED
FROM	
					(
					SELECT DISTINCT		ID_NOTICE_CAN         ,
										LOTS_NUMBER           ,
										ISO_COUNTRY_CODE      ,
										CPV_TED = CPV									
					FROM				Proc_TED.dbo.TED_CSV_CAN		
					WHERE				NUMBER_OFFERS IS NOT NULL
					) AS A
;

evidence.description: SQL preparation reads TED contract notices to map FUTURE_CAN_ID and dispatch dates.
evidence.quote:
WITH CN_DATA AS
(
SELECT DISTINCT	A.FUTURE_CAN_ID                                                      ,
				A.ID_NOTICE_CN                                                       ,
				C.CN_DT_DISPATCH 		                                                                                
FROM				
				(
				SELECT			FUTURE_CAN_ID                   ,
								DT_DISPATCH                     ,
								ID_NOTICE_CN = MIN(ID_NOTICE_CN)
				FROM			Proc_TED.dbo.TED_CSV_CN
				GROUP BY		FUTURE_CAN_ID                   ,
								DT_DISPATCH
				) AS A
			INNER JOIN
				(
				SELECT			FUTURE_CAN_ID                 ,  
								DT_DISPATCH = MIN(DT_DISPATCH)
				FROM			Proc_TED.dbo.TED_CSV_CN
				GROUP BY		FUTURE_CAN_ID
				) AS B
			ON	A.FUTURE_CAN_ID	= B.FUTURE_CAN_ID
			AND	A.DT_DISPATCH	= B.DT_DISPATCH
			LEFT OUTER JOIN
				(
				SELECT			ID_NOTICE_CN,
								CN_DT_DISPATCH = MIN(DT_DISPATCH)       
				FROM			Proc_TED.dbo.TED_CSV_CN
				GROUP BY		ID_NOTICE_CN
				) AS C
			ON	A.ID_NOTICE_CN = C.ID_NOTICE_CN
)

evidence.description: Stata preparation loops over Factiva NGO-search files, builds tempfiles, and uses the AUT_1 series as the initial append input.
evidence.quote:
* Import Factiva's raw csv output for the search of negative procurement coverage and mention of an NGO. (The first column is the year, the second column is the number of articles retrieved) 
foreach c in `countries'{
foreach v in `versions' {
        capture confirm file "Factiva Raw Data/`c'_`v'.csv"
        if !_rc {
                import delimited "Factiva Raw Data/`c'_`v'.csv", encoding(UTF-8) delimiter(comma) clear
				rename v1 date
				rename v2 publications
				replace date = subinstr(date, "Start Date: 1 January ", "",.)
				replace date = subinstr(date, "End Date: 31 December ", "",.)
				split date, p(" ")
				rename date1 year
				drop date*
				drop if year!="2010" & year!="2011" & year!="2012" & year!="2013" & year!="2014" & year!="2015" & year!="2016" & year!="2017" & year!="2018" & year!="2019"
				gen country = "`c'"
				gen file = "`c'_`v'"
				tempfile `c'_`v'_NGOs
				save "``c'_`v'_NGOs'"
				display "`c'_`v'_NGOs"
        }
        else {
                display "`c'_`v'.csv file does not exist"
        }
}
}

* Combine data for all countries 
use "`AUT_1_NGOs'", clear

evidence.description: SQL stage 3 joins the Stata-produced local GDP and media tables into SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES.
evidence.quote:
/* Append GDP variables */
ALTER TABLE SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES ADD BUYER_NUTS3 VARCHAR(5),
								    LOCAL_GDP   FLOAT
;
GO

UPDATE SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES SET BUYER_NUTS3 = BUYER_NUTS WHERE LEN(BUYER_NUTS) = 5;

UPDATE			A SET A.LOCAL_GDP = B.LOCAL_GDP
FROM			SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES AS A
			LEFT OUTER JOIN
				LOCAL_GDP_CLEANSED AS B
			ON	A.BUYER_NUTS3 = B.NUTS3
;

/* Append media variables */
ALTER TABLE SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES ADD DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE1     FLOAT,
                                    DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE2     FLOAT,
                                    DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE3     FLOAT,
                                    DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE4     FLOAT					
;
GO

UPDATE			A SET A.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE1    = B.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE1   ,
                      A.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE2    = B.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE2   ,
                      A.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE3    = B.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE3   ,
                      A.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE4    = B.DELTA_MEDIA_COVERAGE4   
FROM			SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES AS A
			LEFT OUTER JOIN
				Media_Coverage_TED AS B

evidence.description: Appendix describes the Factiva query and translated keyword procedure behind media inputs.
evidence.quote:
Section IA6: Methodology to Construct Media Coverage Variables
IA6.1 Negative Procurement Coverage

       First, we describe the construction of our baseline media coverage variable. The purpose of this

variable is to capture any media coverage of negative procurement topics, such as reports on the lack of

competition in tender offers (see Appendix A Section 2 for a list of examples). To do so, we read a large

number of procurement-related news articles and created a list of keywords to identify articles covering

procurement-related topics that are negative in nature (as opposed to, for example, simple news about new

procurement contracts). Below we provide the list of English keywords and search logic we used in

Factiva:



Keywords to identify public procurement topics:

(public* or government) near (contract* or procurement* or tender* or sourcing* or supplier* or vendor*)



Keywords to identify negative topics:

brib*; corrupt*; kickback*; scandal*; crony*; illegal*; expensive*; delay* near (work* or project*); abus*

near (power or role); (excess* or overrun* or exceed*) near (cost* or budget*);

NOT: (without delay* or less expensive or least expensive)



To capture media coverage across the EU, we next had either professional translators or native speakers

translate the above keywords into the national languages of EU countries covered in Factiva.

Finally, we searched across all news outlets in Factiva based on the translated keywords to identify

negative procurement-related articles.

evidence.description: SQL stage 1 joins contract-level hand-collected price and technical award weights by contract identifier.
evidence.quote:
SELECT			CONTRACT_ID_DIGI,
								PRICE_MATTERS = CASE 
													WHEN SUM(PRICE_WEIGHT) >= 100 THEN 1
													ELSE SUM(PRICE_WEIGHT) / 100
												END
				FROM			Proc_AwardCriteriaHandCollected.dbo.AWARD_CRIT_HANDCOLLECTED_CONTRACT_LEVEL
				GROUP BY		CONTRACT_ID_DIGI
				) AS B
			ON	A.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI = B.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI

evidence.description: SQL stage 1 joins lot-level hand-collected award weights by contract and lot identifiers.
evidence.quote:
SELECT			CONTRACT_ID_DIGI             ,
								LOT_NUMBER_DIGI = LOT_NO_DIGI,
								PRICE_MATTERS = CASE 
													WHEN SUM(PRICE_WEIGHT) >= 100 THEN 1
													ELSE SUM(PRICE_WEIGHT) / 100
												END
				FROM			Proc_AwardCriteriaHandCollected.dbo.AWARD_CRIT_HANDCOLLECTED_LOT_LEVEL
				GROUP BY		CONTRACT_ID_DIGI,
								LOT_NO_DIGI
				) AS C
			ON	A.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI = C.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI
			AND	A.LOT_NUMBER_DIGI  = C.LOT_NUMBER_DIGI

evidence.description: Stata maps five-character geographic codes to NUTS3, averages 2009–2014 GDP by region and writes the 2014 row as NUTS3/LOCAL_GDP.
evidence.quote:
keep if strlen(geo_code)==5
replace geo_code=subinstr(geo_code, "EL", "GR",.)
rename geo_code NUTS3
rename year YR
keep YR NUTS3 nama_10r_3gdp_2 
keep if inrange(YR,2009,2014)

* Take average based on pre-period, making the variable time invariant
foreach v in nama_10r_3gdp_2{
bys NUTS3: egen `v'_avg_pre = mean(`v')
}
keep if YR==2014

* Rename variable and retain relevant fields 
rename nama_10r_3gdp_2_avg_pre LOCAL_GDP
keep NUTS3 LOCAL_GDP

SQL stage 1 reads technical award weights from both the contract-level and lot-level hand-collected criteria tables, keyed by contract and lot.
evidence.quote:
/* Weights for technical criteria  */
ALTER TABLE 	SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES ADD TECHNICAL_WEIGHT FLOAT;
GO

UPDATE			A SET A.TECHNICAL_WEIGHT =  
							CASE
								WHEN C.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI IS NOT NULL THEN C.TECHNICAL_WEIGHT
								WHEN C.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI IS     NULL THEN B.TECHNICAL_WEIGHT
							END
FROM			SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES AS A
			LEFT OUTER JOIN
				(
				SELECT			CONTRACT_ID_DIGI,
								TECHNICAL_WEIGHT = CASE 
													WHEN SUM(TECHNICAL_WEIGHT) >= 100 THEN 1
													ELSE SUM(TECHNICAL_WEIGHT) / 100
												   END
				FROM			Proc_AwardCriteriaHandCollected.dbo.AWARD_CRIT_HANDCOLLECTED_CONTRACT_LEVEL
				GROUP BY		CONTRACT_ID_DIGI
				) AS B
			ON	A.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI = B.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI
			LEFT OUTER JOIN
				(
				SELECT			CONTRACT_ID_DIGI,
								LOT_NUMBER_DIGI = LOT_NO_DIGI,
								TECHNICAL_WEIGHT = CASE 
													WHEN SUM(TECHNICAL_WEIGHT) >= 100 THEN 1
													ELSE SUM(TECHNICAL_WEIGHT) / 100
												   END
				FROM			Proc_AwardCriteriaHandCollected.dbo.AWARD_CRIT_HANDCOLLECTED_LOT_LEVEL
				GROUP BY		CONTRACT_ID_DIGI,
								LOT_NO_DIGI
				) AS C
			ON	A.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI = C.CONTRACT_ID_DIGI

actions.description: Resolve the source and database mapping for the supplied full pipeline, then verify each input product, schema, period and producer-consumer handoff before an authorized run.
steps: Identify author-compatible Opentender Batch1, TED CAN and TED CN source inputs, then verify exact historical table schemas, fields, identifiers, country mapping and notice/award coverage before import.

Obtain the EC survey and monitoring-report author-prepared tables and both hand-collected award-criteria tables; document question/response coding, report-derived flags, contract/lot keys and the country transposition dates used in the two Directive tables.
Obtain or identify the Eurostat nama_10r_3gdp workbook and confirm the Sheet 2 geography/year/unit layout, NUTS3 codes and 2009–2014 observations before applying the documented Stata mean transform.

For Factiva, identify the author-prepared exports or obtain the documented compatible exports after confirming permitted entitlement; preserve the country/version file names, v1/v2 columns, all-media/keyword/NGO search variants and 2010–2019 annual coverage. Confirm the AUT_1 NGO seed is present.

Establish one execution root for the relative GDP Raw Data, Factiva Raw Data and temporary-file paths, and configure the empty Procurement database plus the separate read-only Proc_[Data Source Name] databases described in the README.

Record the SQL Server 2017 product/version and exact installed ODBC driver name/version using approved local software metadata; the author package names only the `Procurement` DSN and does not specify a driver version. Do not inspect external DSN configuration or infer connection success from package presence. Preserve the four stages and the table operations summarized in the hashed workflow trace.
validation: At a separately authorized run, confirm every source table/file maps to the expected fields, IDs, country/year coverage and transformation; verify stage 1 creates SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES, stage 2 reads it and writes LOCAL_GDP_CLEANSED plus Media_Coverage_TED, stage 3 joins both outputs, and stage 4 creates the six e(sample) indicators without changing the author samples or estimators.

review_notes: The first source screen's observed stdout was an empty list because its pattern omitted dsn(...); its original argv/cwd/separate-stderr capture was not retained. The saved observation records that limitation. The earlier raw reader display showed generic DSN/table statement text; the corrected structural trace retains only operation, table, source line and line hash, omitting ODBC statement text. No credential value was included in the assessment and no ODBC connection/query was made.

All four supplied programs and the supplied README, datasheet, appendix and dependency checklist were reviewed. The populated input contracts retain all 15 raw/file inputs and all eight frozen checklist dependencies: D0001 and D0006–D0008 are generated stage-2 intermediates, D0002 is the GDP workbook, and D0003–D0005 are the required Factiva file families.

The native sequence is SQL stage 1 → Stata stage 2 → SQL stage 3 → Stata stage 4. Stata writes LOCAL_GDP_CLEANSED and Media_Coverage_TED, SQL stage 3 joins those into SAMPLE_FOR_ANALYSES, and the final Stata program conditions six regression samples in memory.

Public product pages support candidate sources only; they do not verify the historical author data, exact schemas, country/year coverage, hand-collected coding, Factiva entitlement or the table import mapping. The static open of the author-named opentender.eu root returned no readable lines; this is a capture limit, not evidence of absence. The local catalog alias search is metadata-only and its empty results are not evidence of source absence.
The README and datasheet identify the title consistently. Identifiers.txt is documented as final-sample identifiers and is not an analysis panel; no analysis-only route is established.

The first finalizer wrapper invocation launched the controller child but failed while saving its result to a nonexistent directory. The exact observed wrapper exception, read-only submission hash/mode and preserved first output-pair hashes are in probes/finalizer_attempt001_capture_failure.json. The child's return status and separate stdout/stderr were not persisted and are not reconstructed; the corrected controller invocation is captured separately.

Public quote QA checked all five public evidence rows against the observed source/tool returns and retained literal contiguous fragments. The Eurostat quote is now only the exact dataset title; the separate static open returned only a navigation line, so no coverage claim is made from that open. The Factiva quote has no added terminal period. TED, EC and Opentender fragments remain exact; the Opentender page is the current Uganda site and does not verify the historical European Batch1 input.
